newsitem.title: ITALY: Marchers in Rome protest at Italy's 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Marchers in Rome protest at Italy's 1997 budget.

text.p: Italy's centre-right opposition kicked off a mass demonstration on Saturday as thousands of people marched in Rome to protest at the government's 1997 austerity budget.

Centre-left Prime Minister Romano Prodi's austerity budget aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) from the deficit next year to meet the level needed for membership in Europe's economic and monetary union.
The march, which organisers said had drawn up to 300,000 people from around Italy, began in two spots: from the southern Via Tuscolana and from near the Vatican in the northwest.

Centre-right leaders including former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi were due to address the march when its two strands converged at 1800 GMT in the central Piazza San Giovanni in Laterno, a traditional bastion of left-wing protests.
"This square has hosted the great communist statesmen of Italian history. It is ignoble that a capitalist demonstration like today's is held here," one man told Italian television.
Berlusconi has spearheaded several other rallies against the budget, which the opposition has called a rainstorm of taxes, but Saturday's appeared to be the biggest so far.
He blasted the government last Monday when shopkeepers across Italy protested against planned tax increases.

"I'm worried not just for the 1997 budget but for the whole country. Government parties are occupying all the posts of power, we're seeing a hegemony being created," Berlusconi said at a Milan rally held by retailers' association Concommercio.
